subject: Pinegrove Health — post-incident RCA and corrective sprint closure
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@pinegrovehealth.com>
To: david_kim@redwood.com, sre@pinegrovehealth.com
Date: 2028-06-07T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: urgent: inference latency + error spike impacting Pinegrove prod

David / Redwood team,

We saw a significant degradation in response times and a rise in errors starting ~08:45 PDT this morning on our production inference endpoint (model-x-prod). Key points from our monitoring: 
- 3x median latency (120ms -> 380ms) for generation requests between 08:45–09:30
- Error rate spiked to ~6% (5xx & 4xx client rejections) for requests >1k tokens
- Throughput dropped by ~40% at peak, timeouts increased for heavy batches

This is directly impacting patient-facing features — several flows are failing. We opened an internal bridge but need Redwood to triage urgently and provide an RCA + immediate mitigation plan. Please confirm:
1) What changed in your deployment around 06/07 08:30–09:00?
2) Any model/variant rollouts, quantization pushes, or runtime changes?
3) ETA for a temporary mitigation we can expect (rollback, throttling, alternate model)?

We need an exec-level readout and written RCA within 48 hours. I can make time this afternoon for a 30-minute call.

Thanks,
Elena Torres
Head of Product Engineering
Pinegrove Health

--
Pinegrove SRE (sre@pinegrovehealth.com) attached initial graphs to the bridge (referenced in incident-log).

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: david_kim@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: 2028-06-08T15:30:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: urgent: inference latency + error spike impacting Pinegrove prod

David / all,

Interim root-cause and action plan (triage summary):
- Root cause (high confidence): a mis-tagged quantized variant (model-x-q4_compat) was inadvertently promoted to the prod routing pool at ~08:22 PDT. That variant triggers a different kernel path that results in frequent KV-cache misses for sequences >512 tokens, causing higher token-generation time and intermittent OOMs for batched requests.
- Impact: 3x latency increase, ~5–6% 5xx for worst-case batches, throughput drop when backpressure hit.
- Why it slipped through: release gating did not flag the quant-profile mismatch; internal integration tests covered median seq lengths only.

Immediate mitigations completed: 
- 09:10 PDT: rolled back routing to previous stable variant (model-x-v202805) — confirmed by Pinegrove SRE that error rate returned to baseline by 09:35.
- 09:40 PDT: applied request-size throttling for model-x-prod for batches > 4 while we strongly validate quant variants.

Corrective plan (next steps / schedule):
1) Hotfix (today): disable auto-promotion for unverified quant profiles and add a fast validation check in the router (owner: jonas_weber) — ETA: 6 hours.
2) Runtime guard (48–72h): add compatibility checks to runtime to detect mismatched kernel expectations and reject unsafe variants with a clear error (owner: kimberly_park) — ETA: 2 days.
3) Test coverage (1 week): expand release tests to include long-sequence and high-batch scenarios (owner: laura_bennett) — ETA: 7 days.
4) Remediation sprint (2 weeks): backlog items to harden model onboarding, add a canary ramp policy, and instrumentation for prefix/KV-cache anomalies (owners: jonas_weber / eng runtime team).

I have prepared a draft RCA PDF (Pinegrove-RCA-20280609.pdf) with traces, timeline, and verification steps. Recommend an executive readout tomorrow 16:00–16:30 PDT to walk Pinegrove through findings and the 2-week remediation plan.

Open questions for execs: 
- Do we want to offer a formal SLA credit or a one-time technical credit to Pinegrove? Finance/Sales input needed.
- Do we accelerate dedicated capacity for them as a temporary safety valve?

I'll attach the RCA draft to the next thread.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Director, Site Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: david_kim@redwood.com
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@pinegrovehealth.com>, Pinegrove SRE <sre@pinegrovehealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: 2028-06-09T18:31:00-07:00
Subject: Pinegrove incident - exec readout summary and next steps

Elena — thank you for the bridge and for the patience while we completed the analysis. Short summary and commitments from Redwood: 

What happened (short): 
- A quantized model variant accidentally entered the routing pool; the variant used a kernel path not validated for long sequences. That mismatch caused elevated KV-cache misses and intermittent runtime OOMs for large batches, producing the latency and error symptoms you observed.

Immediate actions completed: 
- We rolled back the variant at ~09:10 PDT on 06/07 (error rate returned to baseline by 09:35).
- We temporarily throttled large batches and placed a hold on auto-promotions for unverified quant profiles.

Commitments (what we'll deliver): 
- Hotfix: router-level compatibility check to block mismatched quant profiles (ETA: 6 hours from 06/08 triage, deployed).
- Runtime guard: reject unsafe kernel/quant combos and provide clear diagnostics (ETA: 48–72 hours).
- Test expansion & remediation sprint: guaranteed 2-week sprint to harden model onboarding, canary ramping, and observability for KV/cache anomalies.
- Written RCA delivered: attached Pinegrove-RCA-20280609.pdf with timeline, traces, and verification plan.

Requested from Pinegrove: please confirm whether you want an executive-level credit or an operational credit for the incident (we are ready to discuss options).

Next steps:
- Action items assigned and tracked in JIRA SUP-9834 (link in thread).
- Exec readout completed on 06/09 16:00 PDT (recording and deck linked in the drive folder).
- We will provide a status update at the end of the remediation sprint and an interim health report after the runtime guard work is complete (target: 72h).

Marissa will keep you posted and is your point of contact for scheduling and follow-through.

Sincerely,
David Kim
VP, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
